title: Reading an Array Entry
statement: Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $a,N,\mathrm{top},i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $l$ be a list of integers, and let $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry is $\mu(a+j)$ for every $j<N$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. Then the value $\mu(a+i)$ equals the $i$th entry of $l$ when $i<N$; equivalently, it equals the default value $0$ if that index is out of range.
hypotheses_covered: The list records μ(a+j) at each index j<N
